A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FARMS study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR100 training, LLM pruning, SciML fine-tuning, and synthetic matrix and teacher–student experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including measured accuracies, perplexities, fine-tuning errors, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 retains fixed-aspect-ratio sliding-window subsampling, pooled eigenvalue analysis, and the same CNN aggregation procedure. Replacing “concatenating” with “merging” and clarifying the SVD diagram do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR100, WikiText, the same seven zero-shot tasks, and PDEBench 2DCFD. The random-initialization, matrix-shape, and teacher–student scenarios in the appendices are also retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain AlphaPruning and uniform pruning with Magnitude, Wanda, and SparseGPT; TempBalance and cosine annealing for image classification; and TB Sigmoid and uniform fine-tuning for SciML. Appendix comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, model configurations, metrics, pruning ratios, calibration sample size, 200-epoch image-classification training, and SciML data fractions are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same experimental settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the layer-selection comparisons, aspect-ratio and sampling-window ablations, CNN aggregation comparison, learning-rate sensitivity, computational-cost analysis, pruning-stability analysis, and teacher–student study. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both specify six calibration seeds, 0–5, for Wanda/SparseGPT in Table 1 and three image-classification seeds, 43, 37, and 13, in Appendix F. Standard-deviation and error-bar reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are retained throughout the main text and appendices. For example, both report Table 1's LLaMA-7B SparseGPT comparison at 0.8 sparsity as 96.02±1.59 versus 79.42±3.86, and Figure 14's correlations as −0.89 for FARMS and −0.51 for the baseline.

T1.justification: The power-law and Hill-estimator equations, Marchenko–Pastur definitions, and feature-spike reasoning are unchanged. Appendix B's new footnote explains the existing transpose and reciprocal aspect-ratio conventions without introducing a new definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The core claims remain aspect-ratio bias mitigation and improved layer-wise training and pruning across CV, SciML, and LLM applications. The headline 17.3% perplexity reduction is unchanged; the new “heterogeneous layer types” wording clarifies the existing motivation.

C2.justification: The interpretations involving improved layer balance and preservation of feature spikes remain intact. Both retain the computational-overhead discussion and caveats about lost correlations and partial matrix coverage in Appendices C.7 and E.2–E.3; local explanatory edits do not substantively change these interpretations.

D1.justification: The code-access link, hardware and timing disclosures in Appendix C.7, and optimizer, learning-rate, pruning, and subsampling details in Appendix F remain unchanged. The clarified covariance convention was already specified mathematically in v1.

R1.justification: Appendix C.3 removes the VQA-related citations used to motivate model selection, while Appendix E.1 removes model-merging and reinforcement-learning examples and their references. Central HT-SR and Tensor Programs positioning remains; numerous other reference edits merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the abstract, introduction, Hill-estimator terminology, experimental explanations, and Appendix E.1. The section structure is largely retained, although Section 4.4 is retitled and the generic Impact Statement and funding acknowledgment are removed.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains matrix-dimension labels, and Figure 3 clarifies per-submatrix SVD and moves beside Section 3.3. Figures 2 and 8 receive caption edits, and several displays are resized or repositioned. All figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The new Appendix B footnote and clearer diagram labels reduce ambiguity about matrix orientation and per-submatrix SVD. Targeted editing improves explanation while preserving the empirical evidence and reproducibility details. Smaller displays and removal of the funding acknowledgment are modest drawbacks; the overall gain is limited clarity.
